short: Micro-ECoG word classification (M05, M06) departs from the 2010 intracortical formant decoders but is standard: one patient, one split, electrodes and trials selected on evaluation data.
position: The paper [@kellis2010decoding] changes two components, both standard under the verdict rules. Its sensors (M05) replace the only prior design in the ledger, a penetrating intracortical electrode (2 of 2 prior studies, Appendix), with 1-mm surface micro-ECoG; its decoder (M06) replaces continuous formant regression with closed-set word classification. Neither is new as a design, since the authors cite high spatial resolution ECoG phoneme classification (Blakely et al. 2008, ref. 31) and their own EMBC 2010 word report (ref. 47), and neither is repeated beyond one patient and one 15/15 split. The strongest confound is selection on the evaluation data: trials were kept only if judged stereotyped, more than half discarded for some words (Sec. 2.2), and the best five electrodes, chosen by overall accuracy with no separate selection set (Sec. 3.3), carry gains of up to 20.0 percentage points. That micro-scale recording matters is untested: the clinical grid in the same patient was not decoded (Sec. 2.1, 2.3).
